summary: The finding holds. I read the policyengine-us 2.15.17 source, and the federal SALT deduction takes its state income tax part from a formula estimate of withholding computed from federal AGI. It does not use the household's state liability. Working without the engine, I rebuilt the five withholding estimates from the scenario inputs and the 2026 parameters, and each matches the sweep to within 0.1 cent. For 081, 0.05 x (174,088.1176 - 4,400) = 8,484.4059. I also rebuilt federal income tax before refundable credits for 022, 081 and 114 under the reference, liability and zero readings, and all nine values match the engine to the cent. Each change equals the household's marginal rate times the change in SALT; the QBI taxable-income cap, the senior deduction and the itemize-or-not choice never bind. On the iteration: every household and reading converged on the first pass (300 of 300), so the fixed-point loop never actually had to iterate. Among the five states, the only channels by which state tax could depend on SALT are the federal itemization flag, Virginia above its applicable amount, and California's dependent-care credit. None of them applies to these households. I found no error in the numbers. The corrections are caveats: (a) the liability readings for 022 and 081 use engine state liabilities that the frozen run already excludes as engine defects; the proposed notes say so; (b) the variable's label is misleading; (c) one Montana formula reads its own withholding estimate directly, so the sweep's override would not reach it. None of these changes which outputs move.

findings.claim: The reference SALT uses the withholding estimate, not state liability.
findings.evidence: Path through the 2.15.17 code: salt_deduction.py:16 takes salt and caps it at salt_cap (lines 22-23). salt.py:11 adds the list in sources.yaml:3-5, which is [state_and_local_sales_or_income_tax, real_estate_taxes]. state_and_local_sales_or_income_tax.py:13-17 returns max(state_withheld_income_tax + local_income_tax, state_sales_tax + local_sales_tax). state_withheld_income_tax.py:10 has no formula: it adds the 44 per-state *_withheld_income_tax variables listed in parameters/gov/states/household/state_withheld_income_tax.yaml:6-54. Each per-state formula reads only adjusted_gross_income_person and parameters: ma_withheld_income_tax.py:13-19, ca:13-17, va:13-17, md:13-47, ct:13-19. In all five baselines, state_and_local_sales_or_income_tax equals state_withheld_income_tax and differs from state_income_tax_before_refundable_credits: CA 6,058.85 vs 2,505.87; MA 8,484.41 vs 8,238.41; VA 5,367.30 vs 3,514.15; MD 15,791.66 vs 6,936.88 + 4,358.51 county; CT 12,010.05 vs 11,917.18.

findings.claim: salt_cap and the taxable-income limit do not change the result for the five households, except that the cap binds for 078 in the reference.
findings.evidence: salt_cap.py:13-25: cap 40,400 single for 2026, cut by 30% of MAGI above 505,000, with a 10,000 floor (values read from the reference parameter tree). All five AGIs are below 235,000, so the cap is 40,400. salt_deduction.py:17-21 also limits SALT to AGI minus exemptions, which never binds. In 078 the reference SALT of 42,251.66 exceeds the cap and is cut to 40,400. Under the liability reading SALT is 37,755.39, below the cap: 0.24 x 2,644.61 = 634.71, which matches the sweep.

Hand AGI = 175,002 + 110.1176 + 56 - 1,080 = 174,088.1176 (engine float32: 174,088.125). part_b.yaml gives 0.05 from 2020 on; exemptions/personal.yaml gives SINGLE 4,400 from 2015 on; no convention touches either. 0.05 x 169,688.1176 = 8,484.4059 (sweep 8,484.4062). Gap to the engine's MA liability: 8,484.41 - 8,238.41 = 246.00 = 5% x 4,920. Reading ma_part_b_taxable_income_deductions.py:45-50, the liability taxes Part B income without netting the $1,080 short-term loss and subtracts $6,000 of deductions (FICA plus rent). I did not read the cap parameters for those two deductions.

findings.evidence: Hand AGI = 91,524.4121 + taxable SS 17,624.75 (0.85 x 20,735, capped) = 109,149.1621. latest_c_ca_hold_2025.py:97 sets the standard deduction to 5,706; lines 53-61 hold the 2025 bracket thresholds; the rates come from rates/single.yaml. Taxable income 74,552.59 on the 2026 brackets (12,400/50,400/105,700/201,775...) gives 11,113.57. Liability reading: SALT 11,334.87, taxable income 78,105.58, tax 11,895.23. Zero reading: SALT takes sales tax 1,155.60, giving 9,984.60, taxable income 79,455.85, tax 12,192.29. All match the engine to within 0.1 cent. Delta = 0.22 x 3,552.98 = 781.66.

The auto-loan interest deduction phases out completely (engine 0). QBI deduction = 0.2 x 6.2225 of REIT income = 1.24. Taxable income 143,059.47 gives 17,966 + 0.24 x 37,359.47 = 26,932.27. findings.claim: 114 federal income tax before refundable credits: reference 10,729.61, liability 11,137.31, zero 11,758.09.
findings.evidence: Itemized deductions = SALT 9,431.59 + charitable 10,913.78 + medical 4,441.86 = 24,787.23. Medical: 10,000 + 2,434.80 of modeled Part B = 12,434.80, minus the 7,992.94 floor. Senior deduction = 6,000 - 0.06 x 31,572.57 = 4,105.65. QBI deduction = 0.2 x 24,361.77 = 4,872.35, against a cap of 15,535.94; taxable income is far below the 201,750 phase-out start. Taxable income 72,807.33 gives 10,729.61. Liability reading: taxable income 74,660.49, tax 11,137.31. Zero reading: SALT 4,756.69 (sales tax 692.40), taxable income 77,482.23, tax 11,758.09. Under zero the household still itemizes: 20,112 vs 18,150 + 1,000 non-itemizer charitable deduction. Delta = 0.22 x 1,853.15 = 407.69.

findings.claim: Neither the QBI taxable-income limit nor anything else interacts with itemized deductions enough to bend the deltas.
findings.evidence: taxable_income_less_qbid.py:14-32 subtracts itemized deductions, so the QBI cap (20% of taxable income) does move with SALT. In every reading the cap stays between 15,092 and 30,138, far above 20% x QBI (910, 1.24 and 4,872.35). The SSTB/W-2 phase-in starts at 201,750 of taxable income. The senior deduction depends only on MAGI (additional_senior_deduction_magi.py:16-26). The charitable and medical floors depend on AGI only. The OBBBA 2/37 itemized limitation (itemized_taxable_income_deductions_reduction.py:26-39) applies only above 640,600. The itemize choice compares federal income_tax between branches (tax_unit_itemizes.py:15-36, tax_liability_if_itemizing.py:11-17) and never flips. So each delta is exactly the marginal rate times the change in SALT; 120 under zero crosses from the 24% into the 32% bracket, and the sweep's 3,203.27 is consistent with that.

findings.claim: Only five outputs move, and no other output changes by even a cent; the baseline reproduces all 1,928 scored references.
findings.evidence: From sweep_salt_withholding.csv: 1,984 rows, 56 excluded. The maximum |baseline - reference| over scored rows is 0.0. In each of the three readings exactly five rows have |delta| > 0.005, all federal_income_tax_before_refundable_credits for 022/078/081/114/120, and the maximum |delta| among all other rows is exactly 0.0. Only 9 of 100 households itemize, and 4 of those have $0 federal tax.

findings.claim: The iteration in sweep_salt_withholding.py is sound, and for these states the liability is not circular in practice.
findings.evidence: sweep_salt_withholding.py:139-149 computes state + MD county - NYC (net also subtracts refundable credits, floored at 0); lines 197-212 run the fixed point with tolerance 0.005 and at most 25 iterations. All 100 households converged at iteration 1 for both liability and net (I counted from the households JSON), so the loop never had to iterate. Channels by state: MA's medical exemption (ma_part_b_taxable_income_exemption.py:36-40) depends only on the federal itemize flag; its charitable deduction (ma_part_b_taxable_income_deductions.py:42) uses the federal charitable deduction, which has no SALT term. CA itemized deductions = itemized_deductions_less_salt + real_estate_taxes (ca_itemized_deductions_pre_limitation.py:16-20), so no state income tax enters; the CA dependent-care credit reads federal income_tax_before_credits (ca_federal_capped_cdcc.py:17), but 022 has no dependents. VA adds and then subtracts state_and_local_sales_or_income_tax (va_itemized_deductions.py:17-33), so it cancels below the applicable amount (332,700 single in 2025, versus 114's AGI of 106,573); only above that amount does va_reduced_itemized_deductions.py:89-98 make it circular. MD uses itemized_deductions_less_salt + capped_property_taxes (md_itemized_deductions.py:20-24) plus the federal itemize flag (md_deductions.py:29-30). A grep finds no CT read of federal SALT or federal tax. Elsewhere, CO (co_state_addback.py:18) and MO (mo_net_state_income_taxes.py:27) read state_withheld_income_tax directly and are genuinely circular, which is what the iteration handles; but the CO/MO households do not itemize.

findings.claim: Montana's federal-tax deduction reads mt_withheld_income_tax directly, so the sweep's tax-unit override does not reach it.
findings.evidence: mt_federal_income_tax_deduction_for_federal_itemization.py:23-26 returns min(mt_withheld_income_tax, cap) as a 'federal income tax deduction'. That person-level variable is not replaced when the sweep sets the tax-unit state_withheld_income_tax. It has no effect here: the only MT household, scenario_100, has $0 withholding and does not itemize. Whether this variable is live in 2026 Montana law is unverified.

findings.claim: The override also feeds benefit-program deductions.
findings.evidence: state_withheld_income_tax is also read by spm_unit_paycheck_withholdings.py:13, ca_scc_general_assistance_earned_income_deductions.py:26, the CA Riverside general relief sources.yaml:4, and the IL AABD exemption sources.yaml:4. Setting the input therefore changes those too. No scored output moved (max delta 0.0), so the result is unaffected.

findings.claim: state_withheld_income_tax carries the label 'state income tax before refundable credits'.
findings.evidence: state_withheld_income_tax.py:7 uses that label, but the variable is the AGI-formula withholding estimate. The mislabel invites exactly the misreading this finding corrects, so any write-up should name the formulas, not the label.

findings.claim: The liability-reading alternatives for 022 and 081 use engine state liabilities that carry known defects.
findings.evidence: reference_exclusions.json already excludes 022's state output (r11_ca_itemized_conformity: frozen 2,439.65, alternative 1,968.81 on 1.755.4) and 081's (r22_ma_part_a_loss_offset: corrected 8,232.90). The proposed records disclose both. My hand recompute with the corrected 081 liability gives 26,992.6335, or 26,992.6352 with the engine's float32 AGI. That is $26,992.63 rather than the stated $26,992.64, a sub-cent rounding effect. For 022, a corrected CA liability (an approximation I did not run on 2.15.17: about 2,035) would put the alternative near 11,999 rather than 11,895.23. The direction stated in the note is correct, since the corrected liability is still above the 1,155.60 sales-tax alternative.

corrections_required: scenario_081 proposed note: with the corrected MA liability (8,232.90) the hand value is $26,992.63; $26,992.64 comes from the engine's float32 AGI (26,992.6352). Either value is fine, but say which precision it uses.

In any write-up, do not quote the variable's label: state_withheld_income_tax.py:7 calls it 'state income tax before refundable credits', but it is the sum of the per-state formula withholding estimates listed in parameters/gov/states/household/state_withheld_income_tax.yaml.

The sweep's write-up should say the fixed-point iteration never had to iterate: 300 of 300 household-readings converged on the first pass. Among these five states, the only ways state tax could depend on SALT are the federal itemization flag, Virginia above its applicable amount, and California's CDCC cap, and none applies to the itemizing households. Saying 'iterated to a fixed point' without this overstates what the iteration did.

Optional caveat for scenario_022's alternative value: the liability reading inherits the r11 California itemized-deduction defect, so a corrected CA liability would put the alternative near $11,999 (my estimate, not run on 2.15.17) rather than $11,895.23. The exclusion decision does not change.
follow_ups: Check whether mt_federal_income_tax_deduction_for_federal_itemization (variables/gov/states/mt/tax/income/deductions/itemized/federal_itemization/mt_federal_income_tax_deduction_for_federal_itemization.py:23) is live for 2026. If so, it is an engine defect: it uses Montana's own withholding estimate as the federal-tax deduction. It is also a gap in any override that sets only the tax-unit state_withheld_income_tax.

Consider an upstream policyengine-us issue: the federal SALT income-tax part comes from AGI-formula withholding proxies (state_withheld_income_tax.yaml), and the variable's label wrongly reads 'state income tax before refundable credits'.
If an exact alternative value is wanted for scenario_022 under a corrected California liability, port r11_ca_itemized_conformity_v2 to 2.15.17 and rerun the liability reading.

summary:
I built a separate harness from scratch and it confirms the finding exactly. It does not import or copy sweep_salt_withholding.py, and it uses a different mechanism. The main sweep sets the tax-unit input state_withheld_income_tax. Mine sets the per-person input <st>_withheld_income_tax on the tax-unit head and 0 on every other member. For the "liability" reading I built the state amount independently: I grouped the reference system's gov.states.household.state_income_tax_before_refundable_credits list by state prefix, dropped NYC (which already reaches SALT through local_income_tax), and added md_local_income_tax_before_refundable_credits for Maryland. Each household was iterated to a fixed point from two starting values, the baseline liability and 0.

Reproduction checks, all 100 households on policyengine-us 2.15.17 / core 3.32.8 with latest_final:
- My baseline matches all 1,928 scored references in reference_outputs.csv exactly (max |diff| 0).
- Against sweep_salt_withholding.csv, my baseline, liability and zero values are bit-identical to the main sweep for all 1,984 outputs (max |diff| 0.0 in each column). No output differs by more than $0.01.

Moved outputs: the set moving by more than $1 against baseline is identical to the main sweep's under both readings, and it is the same five under each. All five are federal_income_tax_before_refundable_credits:
- 022 CA: 11113.57 -> 11895.23 (liability) / 12192.29 (zero)
- 078 MD (already excluded): 24164.46 -> 24799.16 / 27290.70
- 081 MA: 26932.27 -> 26991.31 / 28763.81
- 114 VA: 10729.61 -> 11137.31 / 11758.09
- 120 CT (already excluded): 40416.67 -> 40438.95 / 43619.93

No other output changes by more than 1e-9.

The per-household withholding at the fixed point equals the main sweep's "withheld" value in all 100 households. Changing the withholding input never changes any state's liability (max change 0 across 79 households in states that have a withholding variable). So the fixed point is reached at once (1 iteration from the baseline start, at most 2 from 0) and is the same from both starts.

Montana question: mt_federal_income_tax_deduction_for_federal_itemization is the only thing that reads a per-state withholding variable directly, so it is where the two mechanisms could differ. It cannot change any output. Its chain ends at state_itemized_deductions, which no variable or parameter in 2.15.17 reads. For the only MT household (scenario_100) the withholding estimate and the MT liability are both 0. A diagnostic run of that household with the tax-unit mechanism gave identical outputs.

findings.claim: Montana reads mt_withheld_income_tax directly, so the two mechanisms could differ there, but this cannot affect any output
findings.evidence: grep over variables/ and parameters/: the only direct reader of a per-state withholding variable is mt_federal_income_tax_deduction_for_federal_itemization.py:23. It feeds mt_itemized_deductions_for_federal_itemization_{indiv,joint} and then state_itemized_deductions.py:29-30. grep -w finds no reader of state_itemized_deductions in 2.15.17 variables or parameters, and the README in federal_itemization/ says these files 'are not applied in the final Montana income tax calculation'. For the only MT household (scenario_100) the mt_withheld estimate is 0 and the MT liability is 0. A tax-unit-input diagnostic run of scenario_100 gave outputs identical to mine.

findings.claim: Readers of the tax-unit state_withheld_income_tax see the same value under both mechanisms
findings.evidence: The tax-unit readers are CO co_state_addback, MO mo_net_state_income_taxes, spm_unit_paycheck_withholdings, the CA SCC GA deduction, CA Riverside GR sources and IL AABD sources. My mechanism makes the tax-unit sum equal the main sweep's input. In practice: CO 043 has 0 withholding, and MO 093 (formula 3408.52 vs liability 3388.25) does not itemize under any reading. No state output moves.

findings.claim: The 'minus NYC' adjustment and states without a withholding variable do not affect results here
findings.evidence: Not a defect; a coverage limit of the test data. No household has a nonzero local_income_tax or NYC tax, so the NYC branch is never exercised. 21 households (TX, FL, WA, NH, SD) have no <st>_withheld_income_tax variable, and every one has a state liability of 0, including the WA capital-gains and NH entries in the state list. The two mechanisms are therefore equivalent on this sample but untested for NYC, WA or NH tax.

findings.claim: Only five federal outputs move
findings.evidence: Context, not a contradiction: six households itemize and see their SALT deduction change. The sixth, scenario_072 MI, drops from 973.28 to 814.00 under both readings because sales tax takes over, but its federal income tax before refundable credits is 0 in every reading, so no output moves. Of the remaining households in states with a withholding variable, under liability: 46 keep the same income-or-sales maximum, 26 change SALT but take the standard deduction both ways, and 1 (005) is held at the SALT cap (household_channels.csv).

follow_ups: The 'net' reading was not checked independently; this role covered only liability and zero.

No household in the 100 has NYC or other local income tax, or WA/NH state tax, so the NYC-exclusion and missing-withholding-variable cases are untested by these data. Any future household set with NYC residents should re-check that liability excludes NYC tax, which reaches SALT through local_income_tax.

summary:
I could not refute the proposal. The rule in policybench/reference_exclusions.py requires excluding these outputs, but the records and the release need corrections first.

The strongest counter-argument is that the published record has already accepted the withholding proxy as part of how the reference is computed, more than once, and on purpose:
- On 2026-09-22, convention c_ca_hold_2025 regenerated scenario_022's federal reference through the proxy (11,131.33 -> 11,113.57). The audit traced the path ca_withheld_income_tax -> state_withheld_income_tax -> salt in reference_audit/2026-09-22/verification/v5a_projection_irs_wi_id_ca.md:243-269, and line 7 of that file says the audit "preserve[s] ... withholding/local-sales proxies".
- Also on 2026-09-22, c_md_2026 regenerated scenario_078's federal reference. Sidecar revision[6] is labelled "federal tax through the Maryland withholding proxy". latest_c_md_2026.py names md_withheld_income_tax as the only live reader of the allowance it sets.
- The paper (paper.txt:1041) says Maryland's withholding allowance "reaches federal tax through the state and local tax deduction". The 078 and 120 records describe the proxy without flagging it.

On top of that, the prompt contract (policybench/prompts.py:19-22: "Treat any unlisted numeric input as 0 ... Do not infer unlisted ... expenses") arguably settles the question as zero paid. On that view this is a wrong reference to regenerate, not an ambiguity. And the proposal's own alternative values leave out deductible state payroll contributions.

None of this saves the frozen reference:
- The prior acceptance was never a ruling on whether the proxy is a valid reading of the facts. The audits only scoped it out.
- The proxy matches no reading a careful filer could take. It applies a rate schedule to the whole federal AGI, including Social Security that CA and VA exempt and non-wage income. 022's proxy is $6,058.85 against the engine's own CA tax of $2,505.87; 114's is $5,367.30 against $3,514.15.
- The weekly-hours precedent matches this case closely: the contract said 0, the engine filled in a value, and the output was excluded rather than regenerated.
- Both readings actually occur. No model hit any of the three references exactly (0 of 46 each). Claude Fable 5 wrote "MA income tax withholding treated as 0". Grok-4.7 and Inkling land exactly on 022's zero reading ($12,192). **Proposed payload.** Checked independently:
- The three outputs, 138 rows, have scored=false, excludedReason=reference_depends_on_unlisted_input and excludedInput set to the state-withholding text. No other field on those rows changes.
- referenceExclusions has 59 entries (31 unlisted-input, 28 engine-defect).
- n is the count of scored output rows per model, unparsed rows included (analysis.py compute_metrics around line 1213 gives n=len(group); summary_by_model sums it into total_n). It falls by exactly 3 for every model, 1928 -> 1925. nParsed falls by 3 for 45 models and by 0 for kimi-k2.6, which never parsed any of the three.
- globalWeights does not change, because it is the population-weight artifact, not computed from the sample.
- Otherwise only aggregates change: modelStats, the federal-income-tax programStats row (n 3772 -> 3634, exact 61.61 -> 63.95), its 46 heatmap cells, and failureModes.
- The published payload and the review copy in Downloads are identical. The unchanged-copy payload matches them except for one model's cost overlay and the annotation fields added at publish time.

**Why 3 of 1,928 outputs move every model by about 0.5 pp.**
- The headline is an equal-household mean over 100 households, so each household is 1 pp of it.
- Output-group weights come from population_weights.json. Federal income tax carries 0.1914, second only to Medicaid at 0.2986. _row_weights_for_ground_truth (analysis.py:313-332) splits each group's weight across that household's rows and renormalizes so a household's weights sum to 1.
- The federal tax row is therefore 0.2134 of household weight in scenario_022 and scenario_081, and 0.2000 in scenario_114. Each was worth 0.2134, 0.2134 and 0.2000 pp of every model's headline, 0.627 pp in total.
- None of the 46 models got any of the three right (0 exact hits in 138 rows). Excluding them removes a certain zero and rescales the household's other rows by 1/(1-w).
- So each model's change is (1/100) times the sum over the three households of S_h·w_h/(1-w_h), where S_h is the model's score on that household before the exclusion. This formula matches the computed change to 1.7e-14. The range runs from 0.420 (kimi-k2.6) to 0.611 (GPT-6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol).

**Always-zero baseline.** paper_results._always_zero_weighted_rates gives 69.980 -> 70.395. GPT-6 Sol's lead over it goes from 25.024 to 25.220 points, so the paper's "70.0" and "25.0" become "70.4" and "25.2".

2. The 135 parsed annotation rows on the three outputs are labelled llm_error. As a result tests/test_paper_results.py:395-402 would fail, and the paper sentence "the rest are answers that never parsed" would become false.

summary: I reran the main sweep's withholding result independently and got the same answer. My harness (scratch harness.py) runs policyengine-us 2.15.17 plus latest_final on Scenario.to_pe_household. Its baseline matches all 1,928 scored references with 0 mismatches. Its liability fixed point equals the main sweep's withheld amounts exactly (max difference 0.0). The liability and zero readings each move exactly the same 5 federal outputs by the same amounts, and nothing else moves by any amount (tested at a 1e-6 threshold). Within the scope I was asked to check, the sweep missed three things. (1) A second engine estimate of an unlisted input sits in itemized deductions: a modeled Medicare Part B premium of $202.90 a month ($2,434.80 a year) for every Medicare-eligible person (30 households). For scenario_114 it moves a scored output the proposal leaves out: VA state income tax goes from 3,514.15 to 3,654.15 (+140.00). It also moves 114's federal output by +535.66 and its proposed alternative value. (2) The 20%-of-state local sales tax proxy (local_sales_tax.py:25-30, "This is not an IRS value") moves no reference on its own. It is, however, built into the zero-reading figures quoted in the proposed notes for 022 and 114, and into an existing record's alternative value (121 federal). (3) Under the liability reading, scenario_078's federal output depends on the Maryland county, which the prompt never states: 24,705.95 to 25,068.44 across 24 counties. The README and the proposed note give only the Allegany default. Consumers that bypass the tax-unit withholding variable change nothing: zeroing each state's own *_withheld_income_tax component instead of the aggregate gives identical values for all 1,984 outputs. No household is in NYC or has another local income tax. The NYC entry in the state output aggregate is a latent definition gap only. Excluding 114 state as well raises every model's weighted exact rate by another 0.054 to 0.078 pp and changes no rank. That comes from the repo analyze CLI run on scratch copies, with the published baseline reproduced.
